checks.method: Compared 0.0214 and 0.0191 (pooled 0.02025) with the protocol's 0.0207 and my independent 0.021023.

checks.check: 5c. Inflation factors: about 2x the family alpha 0.01, about 4x the 0.005 per-comparison level
checks.method: Divided the observed rates by 0.01 and 0.005; checked that the comparisons are indeed identical; looked at single-comparison tail rates at 5%, 1% and 0.5%.
checks.result: ACCURATE. Pooled 2.03x of 0.01 (gradient 2.14x, spots 1.91x) and 4.05x of 0.005 (4.28x and 3.82x). The 0.005 level applies exactly: the two comparisons are identical in all 40,000 trials (neutral and no-mutation are the same construction), so Holm's 2p <= 0.01 is p <= 0.005. 'Equivalently' is fair: it is one rate against two denominators. The 4x figure is the right one for this stress, because a valid test would run at 0.005 here, and the 2x figure understates the miss. Tail inflation is about 1.9x at 0.05 (9.65%), 3.2x at 0.01 (3.19%) and 4.05x at 0.005 (2.03%).

checks.method: Fisher exact and two-proportion z on 428/20000 vs 382/20000; Monte Carlo of |difference| under a common rate; heterogeneity across the four shards; KS tests on the per-trial p-values and effects; reading of the generator code for any preset-dependent term.
checks.result: CONSISTENT WITH CHANCE. Difference 0.0023 (Wald 95% CI -0.0005 to +0.0051); Fisher two-sided p = 0.110; z-test p = 0.102; odds ratio 1.12 (0.98-1.29); Monte Carlo P(|difference| >= 46 events) = 0.106-0.113 under a common rate. Within presets the two 10,000-trial halves agree (gradient 214 vs 214; spots 198 vs 184, p = 0.50) and the four shards are homogeneous (chi-square p = 0.37). The per-trial p-value distributions do not differ (KS p = 0.28; mean effect 0.5004 vs 0.4992). The generator draws counts independently of the preset (the preset enters only through a threshold that every episode exceeds by 1, so activity counts and ranks are the same), so the true gap is zero by construction. A gap this size or larger arises about one time in nine. This does not prove the gap is zero, only that the data give no reason to believe otherwise.

checks.check: 5e. Is the endpoint-2 by-product a deep null, not boundary-size evidence?
checks.method: Read pairedMeanContrast (tools/lib/m4-growth.ts) and the contract (alphaPerPreset 0.005, floor 1); computed the expected false-support rate under noncentral t at the observed mean and standard error.
checks.result: YES. The observed mean excess is 0.005 (gradient) and -0.009 (spots) with SD about 1.0 across trials and mean standard error 1.0, so the true mean is about one standard error below the floor of 1. The test is a one-sided Student bound at alpha 0.005 (critical t = 2.656, 63 df). At true mean 0 the noncentral-t expectation is 0.000193, or 3.85 events per 20,000, and 3 were observed. At the boundary (true mean = 1) the nominal rate is 0.005, about 100 per 20,000, roughly 33 times the 3 seen here (26 times the 3.85 expected at true mean 0). So 3/20000 and its upper bound 0.00039 say nothing about endpoint-2 size at the boundary.

qualifications: Scope of the pass. precisionPass: true means the false-support rate of original endpoint 1 under this one declared synthetic stress is shown to be <= 0.025 at one-sided 95% in each preset. It does not show endpoint 1 is at its nominal size (it is not), does not register the candidate, and does not touch joint power (blocker 2), the eleven development histories, the fresh seed matrix, the freeze and registration, or the user's launch decision. The synthetic generator uses abstract activity inputs ('not physical feasibility'), not the real ecology.

The 'bound on how bad an adversarial dependence could make it' wording in docs/m4-growth-precision-results.md is an overclaim. 0.0191-0.0214 is the rate at one dependence strength (treatment-control rank correlation about -0.62). It is not a worst case. My own sweep (numpy, noise scale varied, other terms fixed, 100,000 trials per point) gave endpoint-1 false support of 0.0055 at rho about -0.04, 0.0217 at -0.61, 0.0293 at -0.88 and 0.0333 at -0.97. By interpolation, the 0.025 envelope would be exceeded at about rho -0.7 to -0.75. Say 'the rate at the declared stress strength' and note that stronger negative dependence would breach the envelope. Near-zero dependence gives the nominal 0.005, as the protocol says.

The 'adequate for launch, given the dependence evidence' position rests on within-seed correlations from only 10-20 seeds in the 2026-09-28 ensemble (the protocol itself says 'context, not proof'). Fisher-z 95% intervals for those four correlations are gradient [-0.45, 0.43] and [-0.08, 0.70], spots [-0.60, 0.66] and [-0.62, 0.64]. The spots intervals reach to about -0.60 and -0.62, i.e. they do not exclude dependence as strong as the stress itself (about -0.62), so the real-data evidence cannot establish that real dependence is weaker than the stress. Their lower ends stop short of the roughly -0.73 region where my sweep crosses 0.025, so I am not claiming the data point to an exceedance. (Pearson r on cumulative activity is only loosely comparable with the rank correlation I swept.) The write-up should present adequacy as a judgment for the user's launch decision, not as an established result, and should keep the 'context, not proof' hedge.

Spots-m3 sits at the low end of the plausible range (z = -1.9, p = 0.058 against my 0.021023 reference). It is not significant, and the two-sided difference from gradient has p = 0.11, but it should be described as 'consistent with', not as a close match, and nothing should be read into a preset difference. Do not claim the preset gap is explained.

Margins are not large for gradient-m3: 428 events against a cap of 463 (upper bound 0.02316 vs 0.025). Under a true rate of 0.0214 the stratum passes with probability about 0.957, and about 0.992 at 0.0207, so this pass was likely but not certain. A true rate above 0.025 would pass with probability at most 0.0478.

The two strata are each tested at one-sided 95%. A statement that both rates are below 0.025 simultaneously has at least 90% joint confidence (Bonferroni), 90.25% if independent. This matches the protocol's rule and is a nuance for wording, not a defect.

What cannot be verified from artifacts: that no interim tally was read before `report` ran, and that report.json was written by the `report` command rather than by hand (its content and the 1e-15 agreement with my independent computation are consistent with the command). I found no evidence against either.

The determinism check used the production code, the same Deno build and the same machine; it checks the logged rows are reproducible, not that the generator is correct. The independent numpy simulation (0.021023) covers correctness of the law. The 124-trial sample is 0.31% of rows; the rest are covered by the receipt/log hash chain, row-level identity and manifest checks.
Process notes unchanged from the protocol and review: master seed 650009003 was fresh against local scans only (coordinator registry unreachable), and a ledger entry exists marked consumed.
I did not verify the joint-power document or the statements about the parent's other nine strata or the 0/200 boundary screens in the results write-up; they are outside this study's data.
findings: F1. Integrity is clean. Frozen manifest in all four shards, one terminal complete receipt each, log hashes match, no locks, 52 of 52 source hashes match (before and after my re-run), exact contiguous partition, 40,000 unique rows, all identities and manifest hashes correct.

F2. Tally reproduced exactly: gradient-m3 428/20000 (0.0214, upper 0.023161), spots-m3 382/20000 (0.0191, upper 0.020770); endpoint 2 supported 3/20000 in each (upper 0.000388), 0 unavailable, 3 joint in each; pooled endpoint 1 is 810/40000 = 0.02025. Holm recomputed from stored p-values agrees on all 40,000 rows. precisionPass: true is correct.
F3. Determinism: 124 of 124 sampled trials (58 endpoint-1-supported, 6 endpoint-2-supported, all four shard boundaries) are byte-identical on all six fields under Deno 2.9.7.

F4. The observed rates agree with the pre-declared estimate. My independent 1,000,000-trial numpy simulation of the declared law gives 0.021023 (CI 0.0207-0.0213); the protocol's was 0.0207. Pooled observed 0.02025 is consistent with both (p 0.29-0.54).

F5. The inflation statement is accurate and the 4x framing is the one that applies: the two comparisons are identical in every trial, so the effective nominal level is exactly 0.005. Observed 2.03x the family alpha 0.01 and 4.05x the per-comparison 0.005 (gradient 2.14x/4.28x, spots 1.91x/3.82x).
F6. The gradient-vs-spots gap (0.0023, Fisher p 0.11, CI -0.0005 to 0.0051) is consistent with chance; the generator law is identical across presets. The four shards are homogeneous (p 0.37).

F7. Overclaim to fix in the write-up: the stress rate is not a bound on adversarial dependence. At rho about -0.88 my simulation gives 0.029 and at -0.97, 0.033, both above the 0.025 envelope, and the 2026-09-28 correlation evidence (n = 10-20) cannot exclude dependence as strong as the stress itself (about -0.6) for spots. The adequacy argument is a judgment, not a result.

F8. The endpoint-2 figure is a deep null: true mean 0 versus a floor of 1 with standard error about 1, test at alpha 0.005. Expected 3.85 false supports per 20,000 (observed 3); the boundary rate would be 0.005. Not evidence on endpoint-2 size at the boundary.
F9. Timeline is consistent: launch 21:21:07Z, shard wall times 3594.7-3958.6 s on one attempt each, last receipt 22:27:06Z, report created 22:27:24Z.

F10. Minor: the working copy now holds uncommitted evidence copies (experiments/m4/growth-precision-v1/{report.json,receipts/,evidence-sha256.txt}) and docs/m4-growth-precision-results.md.
